record.original_question: For a map f_{c,b}, if (p_n) is an infinite family of periodic saddles that are pairwise not homoclinically related, must their hyperbolicity degenerate in the sense that min(|λ_-(p_n)|,|λ_+(p_n)|) tends to 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real parameters $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $b \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$, let $f_{c,b}: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the Hénon map
$$ f_{c,b}(x,y) = (x^2 + c - by,\; x). $$
A periodic saddle of $f_{c,b}$ is a periodic point $p$ of some period $k \geq 1$ such that the derivative $Df_{c,b}^k(p)$ has two real eigenvalues $\lambda_-(p)$ and $\lambda_+(p)$ with $|\lambda_-(p)| < 1 < |\lambda_+(p)|$. Two periodic saddles $p$ and $q$ are said to be homoclinically related if the stable manifold $W^s(\mathcal{O}(p))$ of the orbit of $p$ has a transverse intersection with the unstable manifold $W^u(\mathcal{O}(q))$, and vice versa. Being homoclinically related is an equivalence relation on the set of periodic saddles.

Question: For every map $f_{c,b}$ and every infinite sequence $(p_n)_{n \geq 1}$ of periodic saddles of $f_{c,b}$ that are pairwise not homoclinically related, is it necessarily the case that
$$ \min\bigl(|\lambda_-(p_n)|,\; |\lambda_+(p_n)|^{-1}\bigr) \cdot \text{(equivalently, } \min(|\lambda_-(p_n)|, 1/|\lambda_+(p_n)|)\text{)} \longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{as } n \to \infty? $$
Equivalently, must the hyperbolicity of the saddles $p_n$ degenerate in the sense that $\min(|\lambda_-(p_n)|, |\lambda_+(p_n)|^{-1}) \to 0$ (or, in the original formulation with $\lambda_+, \lambda_-$ understood as the two eigenvalues, $\min(|\lambda_-(p_n)|, |\lambda_+(p_n)|) \to 0$ when one of the eigenvalues becomes arbitrarily contracted)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent list of open problems on Hénon maps (2023, published in Arnold Mathematical Journal 2024) and is explicitly stated there as an open question. No web evidence of a resolution was found; related work on hyperbolicity inside homoclinic classes (e.g., Crovisier–Pujals and others) addresses partial results but does not resolve this specific question for the Hénon family.
